title: Fertilisation and implantation in mammals

draft.title: Fertilisation and implantation in mammals
card: Fertilisation is when a sperm cell fuses with an egg cell. In mammals this usually happens in the oviduct (fallopian tube).
The fused cell is a zygote. It has a full set of chromosomes: half from the sperm and half from the egg.
The zygote divides by mitosis as it moves along the oviduct towards the uterus. This forms a ball of cells called an embryo.
Implantation is when the embryo attaches to and embeds in the wall of the uterus. The pregnancy begins to develop from this point.
draft.remember: Sperm and egg fuse to make a zygote, and the dividing embryo then embeds in the uterus wall.

a.q: Which event produces a zygote in a mammal?
opts: A sperm cell fuses with an egg cell
An embryo embeds in the uterus wall
A zygote divides by mitosis into a ball of cells
An egg cell leaves the ovary and enters the oviduct
a.why: A zygote is the single cell formed when a sperm and an egg fuse. Embedding in the uterus wall is implantation, which happens later to an embryo that already has many cells.
a.clue: A zygote is the very first cell of the new individual.

b.q: A researcher studies a mouse embryo that is a ball of cells in the oviduct, before it has reached the uterus. Which statement about it is correct?
opts: It has formed from a zygote but has not yet implanted
It has not yet been fertilised
It has implanted and is now a zygote
It is a zygote that has not yet divided
b.why: A ball of cells comes from a zygote dividing by mitosis, so fertilisation has already happened. Implantation only happens once the embryo embeds in the uterus wall, so it has not yet occurred. Calling it a zygote is wrong, as a zygote is the single fused cell.
b.clue: Work out which steps come before a ball of cells exists, and which come after.

a.best: A sperm cell fuses with an egg cell

b.best: It has formed from a zygote but has not yet implanted
